newsitem.title: INDIA: India's CRISIL downgrades Pearl Polymers Ltd FD.
newsitem.headline: India's CRISIL downgrades Pearl Polymers Ltd FD.

text.p: India's Credit Rating Information Services of India (CRISIL) said it has downgraded its rating of the fixed deposit programme of Pearl Polymers Limited (PPL) to "FA+" from "FAA-".
The new rating indicates adequate safety of timely payment of principal and interest.

CRISIL said in a statement that PPL is the largest manufacturer of Polyethylene Teraphthalate (PET) bottles, jars and containers in India. The company introduced PET as a packaging medium in India in 1985 and subsequently commenced marketing PET containers in the retail markets under the "PEARLPET" brand name.

Net sales of PPL increased by 29.6 percent from 601.6 million rupees in 1994/95 to 853.9 million rupees in 1995/96 on account of regular capacity additions. The demand for PET containers is estimated to be growing at a rate of about 30-40 percent per annum, it said.
Though the company has a strong business position, the capital structure has deteriorated in the last two years.
Gearing (Total debt/tangible networth) has deteriorated from 0.95 times as at March 31, 1995 to 1.53 times as at March 31, 1996, CRISIL said.

PPL's operating profitability (OPBDIT/Operating Income) declined significantly from 17.6 percent in 1994/95 to 11.9 percent in 1995/96 on account of a sharp increase in the PET chip prices, the primary raw material, during the year. The decline in profitability and increase in gearing has resulted in a decline in the interest coverage (PBDIT/Interest and finance charges) from 3.44 times to 2.18 times in 1995/96.
